Early in a tranquil season, the front-counter team met an ordinary disruption
Routine desk incident report

During the morning intake at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, a traveler arrived with a carrier that did not match the details on the booking note. The carrier itself was sound, but the label on the outside was smudged and the pet entry form lacked a clear contact line. The traveler remained calm, and the line behind the desk stayed orderly. I stepped in to check the booking record, compare the papers, and confirm the pet was fit for the planned travel.

The review showed that the reservation belonged to a couple traveling with a small companion animal, and the animal was present and settled. The welcome team had already guided the travelers through the usual boarding checks, so the main issue was the missing detail on the form. I asked the travelers to verify the pet name, carrier type, and destination skyport in plain terms. After that, I alerted the safety coordinator so the usual hazard check could be completed without delay. No signs of distress, injury, or rule breach were observed.

Handling was straightforward. I replaced the unclear label with a fresh desk copy, updated the file with the corrected contact line, and passed the record to the boarding desk for review. The safety coordinator confirmed that the carrier met the travel conditions and that the pet area in the cabin plan remained suitable. The travelers were told to keep the carrier closed and to remain near the gate until called. Staff kept the tone steady and the queue moving while the paperwork was settled.

Follow-up was completed before departure. The corrected form was filed, the booking note was flagged for extra visual check on future visits, and the front-counter team was reminded to inspect pet labels at first contact. I also asked the welcome team to repeat the carrier check on the next handoff so the same mismatch does not slow the desk again. No further issue arose, and the travelers left the counter with the pet cleared for boarding. Companion Animal Travel Desk
